w: Sixty-plus buildings rebuilt on a 25-hectare site above the richest alluvial goldfield on earth, costumed volunteers minding the shopfronts and posing for photos. Ballarat's first gold-rush decade recreated whole - livestock, carriages, working machinery - with a new precinct now added for Wadawurrung culture.
s: Sixty-plus buildings from Ballarat's first gold decade
_facts: Open-air museum in Golden Point, a suburb of Ballarat, depicting Ballarat's first ten years after gold was discovered in 1851
Complex sits on a 25-hectare site linked to the richest alluvial gold rush in the world
Over 60 historically recreated buildings with costumed staff and volunteers who pose for photos and answer questions
Recreation includes antiques, artwork, machinery, livestock and animals, carriages, all appropriate to the 1850s era
20-year Master Plan has added new national centres for rare trades, gold rush collections and Wadawurrung culture
